path_decisions.rationale: Optimizer lacks win_rate objective (line 160-169 only supports sharpe/sortino/calmar/return); entry filters are the highest-leverage win-rate knob since they control which trades are taken

Trend entry requires ALL 5 conditions simultaneously (AND logic at line 239); RSI overbought=70/oversold=30 defaults are too loose for crypto win-rate optimization; tightening is the simplest param change

Current exit only triggers on trend-reversal signals (line 109-115); triple-barrier method exists (barriers.py) but is NOT wired into strategy templates; early profit-taking exits would directly boost win rate
All proposed changes must pass validation gate; gate.py defaults to sharpe objective (line 41) which conflicts with win_rate optimization — need to add win_rate objective to validation pipeline

candidate_solution.summary: 5 concrete code changes to improve win rate: (1) add win_rate objective to optimizer, (2) soften trend entry AND-logic, (3) tighten RSI thresholds, (4) wire triple-barrier early exits, (5) add win_rate objective to validation gate

change_1.title: Add 'win_rate' objective to StrategyOptimizer._objective_value()
change_1.current: Only supports sharpe/sortino/calmar/return — win_rate is computed in BacktestResult (backtest.py:35) but never exposed as optimization target
change_1.proposed: Add 'objective == "win_rate": return float(result.win_rate)' branch. This allows running optimization with objective='win_rate' to directly maximize the hit rate instead of risk-adjusted return.
change_1.rationale: Currently all optimization (including CPCV and WFO) targets Sharpe. A strategy can have high Sharpe with ~40% win rate if wins are much larger than losses. Targeting win_rate directly enables finding parameter sets that produce more consistent small wins.

change_2.title: Relax trend entry AND-logic to 'at least N-of-M' condition scoring
change_2.current: entries = trend_up & rsi_ok_long & vol_ok & atr_ok — ALL 5 conditions must be true simultaneously, producing very few signals
change_2.proposed: Add a 'min_conditions' parameter (default=4) so entry triggers when at least N of the 5 conditions hold. For win_rate optimization, requiring 4-of-5 instead of 5-of-5 allows more trades while still filtering low-quality setups. The min_conditions param becomes part of the Optuna search space.
change_2.rationale: AND-logic across 5 independent filters is extremely restrictive. In crypto markets, all 5 rarely align. Requiring 4-of-5 doubles or triples signal frequency while each individual filter still contributes quality screening. More trades with slightly relaxed filters typically improves win_rate because the marginal signals still have directional bias.

change_3.title: Tighten RSI overbought/oversold thresholds for higher-quality entries
change_3.current: rsi_overbought=70, rsi_oversold=30 — standard thresholds that allow late-trend entries
change_3.proposed: Set RSI overbought=60 (long entry filter: RSI < 60 instead of < 70) and rsi_oversold=40 (short entry filter: RSI > 40 instead of > 30). These tighter bands ensure entries happen earlier in the trend move before exhaustion. Include rsi_overbought and rsi_oversold in the param_space for Optuna search with ranges [55,75] and [25,45] respectively.
change_3.rationale: RSI 70/30 is standard for equities but crypto has stronger momentum persistence. Entering when RSI is between 40-60 (mid-range) during a confirmed trend means entering before the overbought zone, capturing more of the move. This reduces the number of trades entered at trend exhaustion points where reversal probability is high.

change_4.title: Wire triple-barrier method into strategy templates for early profit-taking
change_4.current: Exit only on trend-reversal signal (trend_down + RSI + vol + ATR all flip). No profit target, no time-based exit. This means holding winning trades until trend reversal, which may give back profits.
change_4.proposed: Add profit_take_pct and max_holding_bars params to strategy templates. In generate_signals(), after computing boolean exits from trend logic, also mark bars as exit if: (a) unrealized profit >= profit_take_pct, or (b) holding period exceeds max_holding_bars. This uses the existing triple_barrier_labels pattern from barriers.py. Suggested defaults: profit_take_pct=0.10, max_holding_bars=20 for trend_following on daily timeframe.
change_4.rationale: The current exit logic waits for a full trend reversal signal, which means: (1) winning trades give back open profits before the reversal is detected, (2) some 'wins' become 'losses' because price reverses while waiting for exit signal. Triple-barrier exits lock in profits early, directly increasing win_rate. This is the single highest-impact change because it converts marginal winners into guaranteed winners.

change_5.title: Add 'win_rate' as available objective in validation_gate and WFO/CPCV
change_5.current: optimize_objective defaults to 'sharpe' — validation pipeline cannot optimize for win_rate even if the optimizer supports it
change_5.proposed: After adding win_rate to optimizer.py, update gate.py default to support 'win_rate' as objective. Also update the GO/NO-GO decision logic: when objective='win_rate', use win_rate >= 0.55 as the pass criterion (matching elliott_wave.yaml target_win_rate). For CPCV, require mean OOS win_rate > 0.50 instead of PBO < 0.5.
change_5.rationale: Without this change, even if the optimizer can target win_rate, the validation gate will still optimize on Sharpe during CPCV/WFO re-optimization, undoing the win_rate gains. The validation pipeline must be consistent with the optimization objective.

notes: Key insight: The system computes win_rate (backtest.py:150) but never uses it as an optimization target. The entire optimization + validation pipeline is Sharpe-focused. This means the system is architecturally biased toward risk-adjusted return over hit rate. For win_rate improvement, the pipeline must be re-targeted. Additionally, the mean_reversion and volatility_breakout templates have the same AND-logic problem (mean_reversion.py:95 requires RSI+BB+volume simultaneously; volatility_breakout.py:199 requires 5 simultaneous conditions). The changes proposed for trend_following should be pattern-applied to all templates.
